problem:
Which of the following are first-order linear systems of ODEs?

- ${\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}(t)=\operatorname{cos}⁡(t)\,{x}_{1}(t)+2 \\ {x}_{2}^{′}(t)={x}_{1}(t)-{x}_{2}(t)\end{aligned}$
- ${\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}(t)=t\,{x}_{1}(t)-{x}_{2}(t) \\ {x}_{2}^{′}(t)={x}_{2}(t)+t\end{aligned}$
- ${\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}(t)={x}_{1}^{2}(t)+1 \\ {x}_{2}^{′}(t)={x}_{2}(t)\end{aligned}$

feedback.problem:
Which of the following are first-order linear systems of ODEs?

- ${\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}(t)=2{x}_{2}(t) \\ {x}_{2}^{′}(t)={x}_{1}(t)-{x}_{2}(t)\end{aligned}$
- ${\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}(t)={x}_{1}(t)+{x}_{2}(t) \\ {x}_{2}^{′}(t)={x}_{1}^{2}(t)-{x}_{2}^{2}(t)\end{aligned}$
- ${\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}(t)=7{x}_{1}(t)-3\operatorname{cos}⁡(t){x}_{2}(t) \\ {x}_{2}^{′}(t)=-{x}_{1}(t)\end{aligned}$
feedback.worked_solution:
A first-order linear system of differential equations with two dependent variables is a system of equations that takes the following standard form:

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}(t)=a(t){x}_{1}(t)+b(t){x}_{2}(t)+f(t) \\ {x}_{2}^{′}(t)=c(t){x}_{1}(t)+d(t){x}_{2}(t)+g(t)\end{aligned}
$$

where

- $a(t),$ $b(t),$ $c(t),$ $d(t),$ $f(t),$ and $g(t)$ are known functions, and

- ${x}_{1}(t)$ and ${x}_{2}(t)$ are unknown functions (dependent variables).

With this in mind, let's inspect each system:

- System I is a first-order linear system of ODEs since it can be written in the standard form, where

$$
\begin{aligned}a(t)=0, &  & b(t)=2, &  & f(t)=0, \\ c(t)=1, &  & d(t)=-1, &  & g(t)=0.\end{aligned}
$$

- System II is not a first-order linear system of ODEs since it contains the terms ${x}_{1}^{2}(t)$ and ${x}_{2}^{2}(t).$

- System III is a first-order linear system of ODEs since it can be written in the standard form, where

$$
\begin{aligned}a(t)=7, &  & b(t)=-3\operatorname{cos}⁡(t), &  & f(t)=0, \\ c(t)=-1, &  & d(t)=0, &  & g(t)=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and III only".
